claim: For the two-qubit ferromagnetic XYZ Hamiltonian of Gürkan and Pashaev with \(J_z<J_y<J_x<0\), zero magnetic fields, Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya strength \(D\ge0\), and positive thermal energy \(\tau=kT\), set \(a=|J_-|=(J_x-J_y)/2\), \(g=|J_+|=-(J_x+J_y)/2\), \(z=|J_z|=-J_z\), and \(\nu(D)=\sqrt{g^2+D^2}\). Then the concurrence is zero for exactly one closed interval \([D_-(\tau),D_+(\tau)]\). The right endpoint is \[D_+(\tau)=\sqrt{\left[\tau\,\operatorname{arsinh}\!\left(e^{z/\tau}\cosh(a/\tau)\right)\right]^2-g^2}.\]For the left endpoint, put \(u(\tau)=e^{z/\tau}\sinh(a/\tau)\). If \(u(\tau)\le\cosh(g/\tau)\), then \(D_-(\tau)=0\); otherwise \[D_-(\tau)=\sqrt{\left[\tau\,\operatorname{arcosh}u(\tau)\right]^2-g^2}.\]The zero-temperature critical coupling is \[D_c=\sqrt{(z+a)^2-g^2},\]and whenever \(D_->0\) one has \(D_-<D_c<D_+\); if \(D_-=0\), still \(D_c<D_+\). As \(\tau\downarrow0\), both endpoints converge to \(D_c\). Thus the qualitative finite-temperature zero-concurrence interval reported in the source has an exact closed phase boundary, including the high-temperature regime where the separable interval starts at \(D=0\).

correctness.rationale: Direct Gibbs \\(X\\)-state reconstruction yields the two concurrence candidates. Their monotonic dependence on \\(\\nu=\\sqrt{g^2+D^2}\\) gives one low-\\(D\\) extinction and one high-\\(D\\) revival threshold. Exact inverse-hyperbolic inversion, strict comparison with \\(\\nu_c=z+a\\), and low-temperature limits prove the stated interval.
